text:
{
 "iterations": [
  {
   "iteration_number": 1,
   "theme": "Modern dating: approaching, signs of interest, brakes, expectations and the first date",
   "sections": [
    {
     "subtitle": "Guys don't approach girls? A show about a topic nobody planned to record",
     "screenshot_description": "The host in the studio greets the viewers and announces the topic of modern dating",
     "content": "The show **Generacija plus** on Laudato televizija opens with a song, and then the host welcomes the viewers with the greeting „Praised be Jesus and Mary“. He admits that he never imagined he would record about this topic. Nevertheless, the needs of society and the environment in which young people live impose a conversation about **modern dating**, that is, about guys approaching girls, or girls approaching guys.\n\nThe host poses several questions that will run through the whole episode. Is approaching girls a man's job, or should girls also approach them today? How to make first contact with a person? How to see whether things are going in the right direction? Should anything be pushed by force? The introduction admits to being informal: they themselves do not know exactly what they will talk about, but they know they want to talk about approaching.\n\nThe conversation is nevertheless divided into **five phases**. First come **signs of interest**, then **approaching**, then **red flags** (in Croatian „red flags“), then **unrealistic expectations**, and finally the question of what the **first date** should look like. The host notes that without such a concept the conversation would last „until Marija Pljuska“. He begins with the question of how to know that a person likes us, that is, that we like them and that it is time for the first step.",
     "keywords": [
      "modern dating",
      "first contact",
      "five phases of conversation",
      "signs of interest",
      "red flags"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Laudato televizija",
      "Generacija plus"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Must the girl give the sign first? Guys look for a hint, girls cannot sleep peacefully",
     "screenshot_description": "The first guest says that in the guy's place she would try to approach even without a sign",
     "content": "The first guest says that one thing interests her. Guys regularly say that a girl must give them some kind of sign. Many of her friends claim they will not approach a girl if they have not noticed that she is giving them „hints“. She finds this sad. If she were in the guy's place, she could not sleep peacefully if she had not tried something, even without a sign. She admits that it is easy to say this from a female perspective, so she asks the male guests whether they really will not talk to a girl until they get a sign.\n\nThe second guest thinks it is easier and more natural when everything happens in socializing, when people see each other from time to time, and a glance or some contact already exists. If he likes a girl for a longer time, and there are no opportunities to see her, he thinks it is good to approach **regardless of whether there were any steps in return**.\n\nThe third guest thinks that the sign does not have to be so much „significant“ as a **visible, clear openness**. He describes a situation in which the girl does not look in his direction, or quickly looks away. He says he would not approach „out of nowhere“ just because someone is attractive to him, because physical attraction at first sight is indeed good, but behind it there is also character. He would rather ask around a little and get to know the person, and if he sees a possible way through, he would try. What the girl will answer is up to her.",
     "keywords": [
      "sign of interest",
      "openness",
      "first step",
      "character",
      "physical attraction"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Generacija plus"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "We looked at each other the whole evening: what are real signs of interest",
     "screenshot_description": "The guest explains that signs of interest are seen only once a conversation begins",
     "content": "The host distinguishes two situations. In the first, someone sees someone for the first time and decides to act. In the second, people know each other from prayer communities, shared gatherings and mutual friends. At men's gatherings, he says, one often hears the sentence: „We were looking at each other the whole time, she did not take her eyes off me, and she went home and nothing.“ He asks what the real signs of interest are.\n\nThe first guest thinks that a **glance is a legitimate sign**. If people looked at each other the whole evening, it does not have to be imagination. It is possible that on both sides there was simply no courage. The worst thing, she says, is when one sees that something exists, and no one takes a step, so the girl waits for the guy. A glance nevertheless does not give certainty, because the girl may simply have been in his field of vision. Real signs show when a conversation begins, and that is casual communication, not any „wow entrance“. Then one sees whether the girl answers with only one word, whether she continues the conversation, whether she smiles. There are many **verbal and non-verbal signs** that can be read.\n\nThe second guest warns that girls differ. Some have a tendency to please and out of politeness prolong the conversation, just as there are such men. The first guest therefore advises guys to develop awareness of **body language**. Often they have to be endured because no one wants to say „get lost“. If the girl is turned away from him, keeps looking elsewhere, answers with „yes“ and „no“ and does not ask any additional question, this should be understood as a sign that she is not interested.",
     "keywords": [
      "glance",
      "body language",
      "non-verbal communication",
      "casual conversation",
      "courage"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "prayer communities"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "A big guard and physical attraction: are girls waiting for Saint Joseph?",
     "screenshot_description": "The host speaks about girls' big guard and the importance of physical attraction",
     "content": "The host presents an impression he has heard from numerous male friends and acquaintances, especially at gatherings of prayer communities. According to him, **girls have a very big guard** and allow themselves to be won over much less. They wait for „Saint Joseph“, and when he appears, he is not interesting enough for them. He thinks that some girls overlook interesting guys who are nice and good-looking.\n\nThen he speaks openly about the importance of **physical attraction**, which he considers the foundation of every approach. According to his words, a girl cannot be „Mother Teresa“ if she is not physically beautiful to him, because that does not play a role for him. One should not run from the soul, because we fall in love with the soul and live for eternity, but he cannot be with someone who is not physically attractive to him. He emphasizes that in that case there is no sense even in starting contact. Quarrels and reconciliations with such a person would be illusory. He adds that another show could be devoted to aesthetics and „ugliness“, as a philosophical topic.",
     "keywords": [
      "guard",
      "physical attraction",
      "prayer communities",
      "quarrel and reconciliation",
      "soul"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Saint Joseph",
      "Mother Teresa"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Fear of rejection: are girls or guys to blame?",
     "screenshot_description": "The first guest says that a guy who approaches grows in her eyes, even when she rejects him",
     "content": "The host asks whether girls are to blame for weak approaching or whether guys have failed. The first guest says that girls are partly to blame, because some turn rejection into a scandal. They mock the attempt and spread the story, which is ugly and unnecessary. Yet it seems to her that **being rejected is not the worst thing in the world** and that the fear among guys is greater than the real danger of ugly comments. She says she has not yet seen someone mock someone very nastily, especially if the people know each other. A normal girl will not mock. And if a girl is rude, she says, „thank God she rejected you“.\n\nShe herself respects every guy who approaches, even when she rejects him. Such a one grows in her eyes. She feels greater respect toward the one who tried than toward the one whom she sees that she likes, and who has never done anything, because in her eyes such a one is a **coward**.\n\nTo the question of who the real problem is, she answers that girls lack femininity, and guys lack masculinity. She adds that it is not important who started first: „both sides need to work on it.“",
     "keywords": [
      "fear of rejection",
      "respect",
      "femininity",
      "masculinity",
      "coward"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Generacija plus"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Is approaching a man's job? Guests on the girl who approaches first",
     "screenshot_description": "The third guest explains why he thinks a man must take the first direct step",
     "content": "To the question of who approaches first today and whether first contact is exclusively a man's job, the third guest answers that in his opinion it must be a **man**. From personal experience he says that when a girl approached him it was a „big turn off“ for him, because such a character does not suit him. The direct step, like inviting to a date, should be on the man. A woman can **initiate the situation** and make it so that he approaches her, but she should never be direct with words such as „I like you, let's go for coffee“. He adds that today people are closed, even at camps and communities, where the greatest probability is that someone will meet a person of the same convictions. There one should be open and keep in mind that it can happen.\n\nThe host says jokingly that he would ban by law taken people from going to summer camps. He emphasizes that he knows that in the show one should give socially desirable answers, but **personally** he thinks that a woman who approaches a man does so „out of desperation“. He does not want to devalue any woman, but he asks what use is to him a man who must not approach.\n\nThe first guest personally would not act that way because her whole relationship would hang on the fact that she was the one who initiated. Some of her friends, however, told her that it would be great for them if a girl approached them because they would have less work. The host answers that he could not take seriously a girl who approaches him, although he admits that he may be too strict and that this is not a universal rule.\n\nThe second guest agrees that the general rule can depend on the situation. If people are just getting to know each other, move in the same circles or the girl is already interested, she can also approach. But the concrete step of an invitation to an **official date** should be carried out by the man. Personally he found it off-putting when a girl approached him because she liked him, two or three times, and he heard that through others. The fourth participant adds that guys can leave the impression that they like a girl, when they are only too friendly, while girlfriends can „pump up“ a story that does not exist.",
     "keywords": [
      "who approaches first",
      "man's job",
      "initiative",
      "invitation to a date",
      "communities and camps"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "summer camps",
      "church order"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "A message on Instagram instead of words in person: what holds guys back",
     "screenshot_description": "The third guest speaks about courage behind the screen and the anonymity of the internet",
     "content": "The host moves on to the virtual world. He asks why it is easier for young people to send a message on Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat or Facebook than to approach in person, and what holds men back the most today. He also poses the question of how we came to a situation in which a woman must approach a man.\n\nThe third guest emphasizes the **courage that the internet and anonymity give**. Behind the screen a message can be carefully shaped, and this is part of a wider problem of unwillingness to step out of one's own comfort zone. Today there is an option that did not exist before: a man can see a girl in person, and yet write her a message. Before, a letter traveled, so one would think three times. He also thinks that **pornography** influences the male view of woman, and its prevalence does not stop, which is a big problem because of which a man does not approach a woman.\n\nThe second guest adds that the digital age has made us less skilled in practice, because we are in contact with each other much less. There is no naturalness and „flow“, and for people every step has become a „project“. He advises relaxedness: if it happens, great, if not, no problem. The participant points out that these are **social skills** that are practiced less.\n\nThe first guest, however, thinks that social networks are not entirely bad, because many couples came out of them. The host clarifies that they are talking about a situation when one already knows the girl, and not about contacting a random girl. He adds that the one who likes a girl **creates circumstances**. Someone wants to and finds a way, and someone does not want to and finds excuses. The first guest concludes that the answer lies in how much a person really likes someone. If he truly „likes her madly“, he would have approached.",
     "keywords": [
      "online messages",
      "anonymity",
      "pornography",
      "social skills",
      "comfort zone"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Instagram",
      "TikTok",
      "Snapchat",
      "Facebook"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Shame, fear of a relationship and exclusivity: three brakes besides fear of rejection",
     "screenshot_description": "The host lists additional brakes that keep guys from approaching",
     "content": "The host states that men are poorly connected even with other men. According to what he heard from a psychologist, today they do not develop social skills even in the sense of approaching other men. As an example he gives football sessions at which the players barely greet each other, come to play and leave.\n\nBesides the fear of rejection, which the guest mentioned, he adds **three brakes**:\n\n- **Shame.** There are many guys who are ashamed to approach a girl, and do not want to overcome that shame.\n- **Fear of a relationship.** If they approach, a relationship can happen, and it demands readiness for change and sacrifice, renunciation, for which many guys are not ready.\n- **Exclusivity.** According to the host's opinion, the male gaze today is not exclusive toward one woman, because of pornography, social networks and the sea of girls who can be looked at and compared.\n\nThe host claims that the only rule of dating is exclusivity. A man should say: „I am going out with you and I want to see how it will be for me with you.“ He admits that there may be more beautiful, smarter and more pious ones, but he chose her. He believes that God will bless such determination, whether by entering a relationship or by discovering that the person is not for him.",
     "keywords": [
      "shame",
      "readiness for sacrifice",
      "exclusivity",
      "determination",
      "pornography"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "football",
      "God"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Red flags: passivity, rudeness toward the waiter and care for oneself",
     "screenshot_description": "The female guests list what bothers them about a guy already on the first date",
     "content": "The host asks the girls what they consider problematic in a guy, i.e. what their **red flags** are.\n\nThe first guest lists as a big minus the lack of initiative on a date. If a guy invites her, and does not know where they will go and has not planned an activity, that bothers her. Of course, the girl should also participate, but the guy should show masculinity in initiative. Connected with this is **passivity and a lack of ambition in life**. A man should have the desire to find a job, earn and provide for a family. If he does nothing, has no job, and mom and dad give him money, that is not a masculine trait for her and it is very off-putting to her.\n\nThe fourth participant looks at behavior. It is off-putting to her if a guy is not kind and polite to delivery people, waiters, salespeople and others in service jobs, because then it is seen that he is kind only to those from whom he has a benefit. Another thing is **care for oneself**. If he has too much of it, he seems self-satisfied and too focused on himself. If he has too little, the question arises how he will take care of her and the family.",
     "keywords": [
      "red flag",
      "initiative",
      "passivity",
      "ambition",
      "kindness toward others"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Generacija plus"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "What guys look at in girls: family, humble openness and readiness for sacrifice",
     "screenshot_description": "The third guest explains why a girl's relationship with her family is an important indicator",
     "content": "To the question of what men look at in girls, the third guest says that it is very important that she has a **good relationship with her family**, especially with her parents, but also with other members and toward other people. This shows her spiritual background, maturity and goodness. A healthy family produces healthy persons, because we are often a reflection of our parents and their upbringing, and the Lord Jesus changes our lives. What her parents went through and what she went through with her parents, he sees as an important indicator, and something suspicious in that area he considers a „reflex“.\n\nThe second guest says that it bothers him when a girl has **too big a guard**. She can hold to herself and her views, but she should be open and humble enough for normal communication and it must be possible to resolve things through conversation. It is also important that she is eager for sacrifice for a shared relationship, marriage and family, which is often a problem today. Many girls are modern, and some who were raised traditionally, because of modern times, become „neither here nor there“, in transition.",
     "keywords": [
      "relationship with family",
      "guard",
      "humility",
      "readiness for sacrifice",
      "upbringing"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Lord Jesus"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Father figure, too much makeup and difficult opening up after lived wounds",
     "screenshot_description": "The host explains why a girl and her relationship to a father figure are important to him",
     "content": "The host says that when he goes out with a girl it is very important to him what kind of **father figure** she had and how she relates to her father, if she has one. It can also be an uncle, a maternal uncle, a professor or a priest, with the remark that he is speaking of a healthy measure. He explains that a girl who does not know roughly what kind of man should be projects her own idea onto the future man. Thus she drives him to step out of his identity, which leads to ruin. If she does not have such an experience, one moves on to other things.\n\nHis second criterion is **too much makeup**. He admits that this is not a socially desirable answer, but it puts him off, and at weddings in the last two years he has not seen too many beautiful girls.\n\nThird, girls bear lived wounds and traumas with more difficulty, and so they open up with difficulty to a new person. Men, in his opinion, think differently: „There are still fish in the sea.“ Therefore he appreciates it when a girl knows how to communicate how hard it is for her to entrust intimacy, but sees in him someone to whom she will gradually open it. That seems „too beautiful“ to him.\n\nHe also says that he could not be with a girl who has no female friends and is always available on call. He does not want to be an idol in her life nor placed above God. A girl should be **diverse**, have hobbies, friends, activities, a job. The second guest concludes that one can see whether the person was only waiting for someone to come or was really preparing for that moment.",
     "keywords": [
      "father figure",
      "makeup",
      "trust",
      "lived traumas",
      "diversity"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "God"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Standard or ideal? When criteria become too high",
     "screenshot_description": "The first guest speaks about too high criteria and too much choice today",
     "content": "The host poses a question about realistic and unrealistic expectations: whether one should have them at all and whether there is a scale of criteria that a partner should satisfy.\n\nThe first guest says that everyone has criteria, and a person who would agree to anything would be sad. Yet the criteria are often **too high**. With guys this is partly because of content from the internet that spoils the picture of how a woman should look. Girls often string together which traits a guy should have, instead of looking at the real person in front of them and assessing whether they want to be with her. Another problem is **too much choice**: apps, communities, and one comes to Jarun and „each one is more beautiful than the other“. Therefore it is hard to decide on one. She recommends lowering expectations a little, but not below a certain limit.\n\nThe host distinguishes **ideal** and **standard**. The ideal is what one strives for and what one should reach, and the standard is what one does not go below. Then he invites the girls to say what makes a woman feminine, and after that the men will answer what makes a man masculine.",
     "keywords": [
      "standard",
      "ideal",
      "unrealistic expectations",
      "too much choice",
      "dating apps"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Jarun"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "What makes a woman feminine: knowing how to love, being open and gentle",
     "screenshot_description": "The fourth participant explains that femininity is above all the ability to love",
     "content": "The fourth participant emphasizes that primarily a woman **should know how to love**. How this will be realized in all fields of her life, that is what is called femininity. She lists openness toward others, openness to help, being there for listening and knowing how to say the right word at the right time. These are virtues that are received from the relationship with the Lord and grow in a person. Every woman has femininity in herself, but it depends how much she cultivates it and works on it.\n\nThe first guest agrees with gentleness and openness, but warns that every girl **expresses her gentleness in a different way** and that not all need to be „by the same stencil“. She also sees femininity in work on the relationship, in agreeing that the guy leads the matter and in not complaining about every small thing. The fourth participant adds that in a relationship we learn to be submissive to love, which will be realized even more fully in marriage.",
     "keywords": [
      "femininity",
      "to love",
      "gentleness",
      "openness",
      "virtues"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Lord"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "What kind of man he should be: honesty, determination, prayer and standards for Catholics",
     "screenshot_description": "The second guest lists the expectations that Catholics should have in a relationship",
     "content": "The third guest says that a man should be **direct** and communicate his intentions, i.e. where he stands toward the girl and where he plans to go. **Determination** is important, that he does what he said he would do, but also prudence in conversation with the girl and readiness to hear her out when she tells him what she wants to say to him. Most important is that all of this happens with **prayer**. Wishes should be subordinated to what the Lord wants in our life.\n\nThe second guest returns to expectations. There are many personal expectations, but for Catholics there are those on which one does not give way: **openness to faith and shared life in God and openness to life in marriage**. If a person is truly loved, many other personal things can be made to fit, but it is hard to leave a person for reasons lower than that. It can be done without it, but it would be demanding.\n\nA man, according to him, should be clear and concrete from the beginning. He must set things as a standard and a path on which one goes, be active, not passive, disciplined and be a **true example to his wife and children**, God willing.",
     "keywords": [
      "determination",
      "prayer",
      "openness to marriage",
      "faith",
      "communication of intentions"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Lord",
      "God"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Masculinity, responsibility and consistency: a man who does not know how to change a light bulb",
     "screenshot_description": "The host explains his view of masculinity and responsibility",
     "content": "The host speaks about masculinity from the male perspective and first describes the **feminized man**. He invokes St. Thomas Aquinas, who defines this as refusing to do things that are strenuous and hard. In doing so he criticizes men who wear makeup, wear many rings and trousers that reveal the ankles. Some things, he claims, every responsible man should know: change a light bulb, mow the grass, assemble a work desk. Whoever does not know „has no business“ in a relationship.\n\nThe second trait is that a man himself must be worthy of what he seeks. He cannot demand of a partner that she have certain traits if he does not offer value as a „package“. He also warns that people often place value in what they possess (car, job, apartment), and present a partner too as a trophy, and not as a person worth going after.\n\nThe third is **consistency**. A man establishes a moral order in the relationship: one does not cross the line, some things are not talked about, some things are not done. If he is consistent, he grows in authority and integrity. As an example he cites a guy who has a disco ball in his car, and does not repair the air conditioning, or who promises a repair that never comes, „like waiting for Godot“.\n\nThe first guest adds that from small things one sees whether someone will be able to do great things: if he says he will do something today and does not do it, that is an indicator. The fourth participant sums this up with the words „being consistent“. The second guest incidentally retells a joke about a grandmother into whose house a car enters, and the driver says „sorry“ to her, and she answers that she sees that it is „sorry“, but how will he fix it.",
     "keywords": [
      "masculinity",
      "consistency",
      "responsibility",
      "feminized man",
      "integrity"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "St. Thomas Aquinas",
      "Aristotle",
      "Godot"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "The first date: coffee or a walk and how seriously to take it",
     "screenshot_description": "The guests discuss whether coffee or a walk is the better choice for the first date",
     "content": "When the topic shifts to the concrete question of how to approach and what the first steps look like, the host asks whether the first outing should be short or whether an opportunity should be given to see whether it is „the one“.\n\nThe first guest states that people should know that the **first date is neither marriage nor a relationship**. The first coffee we can call whatever we want. People take it too seriously. Nothing will happen if a girl goes for coffee with a guy even though she is not one hundred percent sure. A girl should not think that she promised the guy something, and neither should the guy think that she promised him marriage. Everyone should „cool down a little“.\n\nThe host is against coffee. He thinks that it is an **unnatural environment** for two people who do not know each other. A date easily lasts two to three hours with one drink, and the conversation goes like filling out a „lexicon“: which school did you finish, what do you do, where are your parents from. Leaving a good impression within that framework is hard. A **walk** and more active socializing are more natural to him.\n\nThe first guest notes that on a walk one must talk the whole time, and the second guest that a walk is more intimate because one walks next to each other. The fourth participant would not give coffee great weight as a measure of a relationship because the first coffee can be awkward. The second guest says that coffee is his first choice, but a walk is ten times dearer to him, especially for the second or third time. The first guest concludes that everything depends on how much the people already know each other.",
     "keywords": [
      "first date",
      "coffee",
      "walk",
      "expectations",
      "conversation"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Generacija plus"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "How often to see each other and what the love languages are",
     "screenshot_description": "The second and third guest speak about the frequency of seeing each other and communication in a relationship",
     "content": "The host asks how often a couple in the making should see each other: five times a week or once to twice, and whether there is some universal rule.\n\nThe second guest says that it depends on the couples. For those who are already established, know what they want and are quickly ready for marriage, once to twice a week is enough because of life obligations. Younger ones are often more in love and want more time. In his case a good deal of shared time was needed for things to get moving, because both started from the same position, so seeing each other **three to four times a week** in the initial period was welcome to them.\n\nThe third guest thinks it is useful to talk about this. The person on the other side perhaps perceives only through time spent that we like them. For one, words and compliments are enough, for another quality time is important, i.e. this is about **love languages**. It is important to communicate this, but not to exaggerate: one should not give a gift every time nor use only one love language every time. Everything should be moderate, and a man should be moderate and recognize this in the relationship.",
     "keywords": [
      "frequency of seeing each other",
      "love languages",
      "quality time",
      "moderation",
      "communication"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Generacija plus"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Encouragement to those who are alone: create opportunities, be brave and creative",
     "screenshot_description": "The third guest speaks about creating opportunities and an example with dancing at a wedding",
     "content": "Near the end of the show the host states that a man must gather enough courage and approach a girl, which is a man's job: „Guys, dare, don't be fools.“ He asks about people who are alone and claim that they cannot find anyone, which, he says, is the greatest lie that can be heard about dating. He asks how to encourage them.\n\nThe third guest emphasizes that in his life and surroundings one **should create opportunities**, especially on the female side, where the atmosphere is more closed. He cites a story of a friend from a wedding: after the first dance and a slower song two women get up and dance together. The message is that one should not sit at the table and wait for someone to invite one to dance. Such behavior functions as an **invitation**, and a man likewise must decisively say and do something. One must decide and dare.\n\nThe first guest adds that if you want something, you have to make an effort and „grit your teeth“. It will not fall from the sky. Girls open up and give signals with difficulty, and for guys it is hard to approach, but there is no easy path.
